notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.

notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

% The interpreter of Roulette's scaling/hardware.rkt, ported to ProbLog: a
% loop over a memory of two cells of $2 bits, the total and the counter,
% whose every read first resets the cell to 0 with probability 0.0001
% (z(J, R) before the R-th read of iteration J), running `tri n`: the
% counter starts at $3 (n as `(int n)` holds it in $2 bits), then while
% the counter is not 0, total := total + counter and counter := counter +
% 1, for at most $4 iterations, the fuel; entered with none left, the loop
% ends the run with no result. The cells are bit vectors as Roulette's,
% their set bits atoms: t(J, K) and c(J, K), bit K of the total and the
% counter entering iteration J, on(J) while the loop runs, x(J) when it
% leaves at iteration J. The reads: d (the counter, its test), u (the
% total), g (the counter, its sum), f (the counter, its step). The sums
% ripple their carries up to bit $2 - 1 and drop the last, as bvadd does:
% tx and tc are the total's bit without the carry and the carry into it,
% cc the counter's carry. The queries, consulted from $1 with the totals a
% run can end with (total/1), are res(T) for each of them and res(L), L
% one past the largest, for a run out of fuel (out_of_fuel/1).
% The totals a run of hardware.rkt can end with (the reference's states), the label
% of a run out of fuel, one past the largest, and the queries.
total(0).
total(1).
total(2).
total(3).
total(5).
out_of_fuel(6).
query(res(0)).
query(res(1)).
query(res(2)).
query(res(3)).
query(res(5)).
query(res(6)).
width(20).
start(2).
fuel(3).
step(0) :- fuel(F), F > 0.
step(J1) :- step(J), fuel(F), J1 is J + 1, J1 < F.
0.0001::z(J, 1) :- step(J).
0.0001::z(J, 2) :- step(J).
0.0001::z(J, 3) :- step(J).
0.0001::z(J, 4) :- step(J).
% one(X, K): bit K of the number X is set, for the numbers the program reads
number_read(C) :- start(C).
number_read(T) :- total(T).
digits(X, 0, X) :- number_read(X).
digits(X, K1, R1) :- digits(X, K, R), R > 1, K1 is K + 1, R1 is R // 2.
one(X, K) :- digits(X, K, R), R mod 2 =:= 1.
c(0, K) :- start(C), one(C, K).
on(0).
d(J, K) :- step(J), c(J, K), \+z(J, 1).
nz(J) :- d(J, _).
x(J) :- step(J), on(J), \+nz(J).
on(J1) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, on(J), nz(J).
u(J, K) :- step(J), t(J, K), \+z(J, 2).
g(J, K) :- d(J, K), \+z(J, 3).
f(J, K) :- g(J, K), \+z(J, 4).
% the total := u + g
tx(J1, K) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, u(J, K), \+g(J, K).
tx(J1, K) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, g(J, K), \+u(J, K).
tc(J1, K1) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, u(J, K), g(J, K), K1 is K + 1, width(W), K1 < W.
tc(J, K1) :- tc(J, K), tx(J, K), K1 is K + 1, width(W), K1 < W.
t(J, K) :- tx(J, K), \+tc(J, K).
t(J, K) :- tc(J, K), \+tx(J, K).
% the counter := f + 1
c(J1, 0) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, \+f(J, 0).
cc(J1, 1) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, f(J, 0), width(W), 1 < W.
cc(J, K1) :- cc(J, K), P is J - 1, f(P, K), K1 is K + 1, width(W), K1 < W.
c(J1, K) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, f(J, K), K > 0, \+cc(J1, K).
c(J, K) :- cc(J, K), P is J - 1, \+f(P, K).
% the total the loop left with, and whether it is T
done :- x(_).
r(K) :- x(J), t(J, K).
mismatch(T) :- total(T), one(T, K), \+r(K).
mismatch(T) :- total(T), r(K), \+one(T, K).
res(T) :- total(T), done, \+mismatch(T).
res(L) :- out_of_fuel(L), fuel(F), on(F).

fun step(s: (int(2), (int(2), (bool, (bool, int(2)))))) {
  let t = fst s in
  let c = fst (snd s) in
  let running = fst (snd (snd s)) in
  let finished = fst (snd (snd (snd s))) in
  let r = snd (snd (snd (snd s))) in
  let d = if flip 0.0001 then int(2, 0) else c in
  let x = running && d == int(2, 0) in
  let r2 = if x then t else r in
  let u = if flip 0.0001 then int(2, 0) else t in
  let g = if flip 0.0001 then int(2, 0) else d in
  let f = if flip 0.0001 then int(2, 0) else g in
  (u + g, (f + int(2, 1), (running && !x, (finished || x, r2))))
}
let s = iterate(step, (int(2, 0), (int(2, 3), (true, (false, int(2, 0))))), 100000) in
let finished = fst (snd (snd (snd s))) in
let r = snd (snd (snd (snd s))) in
if finished then (if r == int(2, 0) then int(3, 0) else (if r == int(2, 1) then int(3, 1) else (if r == int(2, 2) then int(3, 2) else (if r == int(2, 3) then int(3, 3) else int(3, 4))))) else int(3, 4)

function shr(x::DistUInt{W}, n::Integer) where W
    k = min(n, W)

components(x::Tuple) = reduce(vcat, map(components, x); init = Any[])

function warmup()
    a = flip(0.7)
    x = discrete(DistUInt{2}, [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4])
    y = uniform(DistUInt{3}, 1, 6)
    z = ifelse(a, x + DistUInt{2}(1), x - DistUInt{2}(1))
    t = ifelse(flip(0.4), (a, z), (!a, x * x))
    e = prob_equals(z, DistUInt{2}(2)) | (x < z) | xor(a, flip(0.2))

module AleaProgram
using Alea
# Julia would spend more time optimizing the long straight-line functions
# below than running them takes: they are interpreted, and Alea's own
# methods compile as usual.
Base.Experimental.@compiler_options compile=min optimize=0 infer=false

const EV = Ref{AnyBool}(true)
observe!(path, c) = (EV[] = EV[] & (!path | c); true)

function shr(x::DistUInt{W}, n::Integer) where W
    k = min(n, W)
    DistUInt{W}(vcat(fill(false, k), x.bits[1:W - k]))
end

components(x::Tuple) = reduce(vcat, map(components, x); init = Any[])
components(x) = Any[x]
width(::DistUInt{W}) where W = W

function warmup()
    a = flip(0.7)
    x = discrete(DistUInt{2}, [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4])
    y = uniform(DistUInt{3}, 1, 6)
    z = ifelse(a, x + DistUInt{2}(1), x - DistUInt{2}(1))
    t = ifelse(flip(0.4), (a, z), (!a, x * x))
    e = prob_equals(z, DistUInt{2}(2)) | (x < z) | xor(a, flip(0.2))
    pr(flip(0.7))
    pr(a, z, y, t...; evidence = e)
    nothing
end

function d_step(x1_path, x2_s)
    x3_t = x2_s[1]
    x4_c = x2_s[2][1]
    x5_running = x2_s[2][2][1]
    x6_finished = x2_s[2][2][2][1]
    x7_r = x2_s[2][2][2][2]
    x8_d = flip(0.0001)
    x9_d = x8_d === true ? DistUInt{300000}(0) : x8_d === false ? x4_c : ifelse(x8_d, DistUInt{300000}(0), x4_c)
    x10_x = (x5_running & prob_equals(x9_d, DistUInt{300000}(0)))
    x11_r2 = x10_x === true ? x3_t : x10_x === false ? x7_r : ifelse(x10_x, x3_t, x7_r)
    x12_u = flip(0.0001)
    x13_u = x12_u === true ? DistUInt{300000}(0) : x12_u === false ? x3_t : ifelse(x12_u, DistUInt{300000}(0), x3_t)
    x14_g = flip(0.0001)
    x15_g = x14_g === true ? DistUInt{300000}(0) : x14_g === false ? x9_d : ifelse(x14_g, DistUInt{300000}(0), x9_d)
    x16_f = flip(0.0001)
    x17_f = x16_f === true ? DistUInt{300000}(0) : x16_f === false ? x15_g : ifelse(x16_f, DistUInt{300000}(0), x15_g)
    x18_step = ((x13_u + x15_g), ((x17_f + DistUInt{300000}(1)), ((x5_running & !(x10_x)), ((x6_finished | x10_x), x11_r2))))
    return x18_step
end

function dice_main()
    x19_s = (DistUInt{300000}(0), (DistUInt{300000}(2), (true, (false, DistUInt{300000}(0)))))
    for _ in 1:3
     x19_s = d_step(true, x19_s)
    end
    x20_finished = x19_s[2][2][2][1]
    x21_r = x19_s[2][2][2][2]
    if x20_finished !== false
     x22_result = prob_equals(x21_r, DistUInt{300000}(0))
     if x22_result !== true
      x23_result = prob_equals(x21_r, DistUInt{300000}(1))
      if x23_result !== true
       x24_result = prob_equals(x21_r, DistUInt{300000}(2))
       if x24_result !== true
        x25_result = prob_equals(x21_r, DistUInt{300000}(3))
        if x25_result !== true
         x26_result = prob_equals(x21_r, DistUInt{300000}(5))
         x27_result = x26_result === true ? DistUInt{3}(4) : x26_result === false ? DistUInt{3}(5) : ifelse(x26_result, DistUInt{3}(4), DistUInt{3}(5))
        end
        x28_result = x25_result === true ? DistUInt{3}(3) : x25_result === false ? x27_result : ifelse(x25_result, DistUInt{3}(3), x27_result)
       end
       x29_result = x24_result === true ? DistUInt{3}(2) : x24_result === false ? x28_result : ifelse(x24_result, DistUInt{3}(2), x28_result)
      end
      x30_result = x23_result === true ? DistUInt{3}(1) : x23_result === false ? x29_result : ifelse(x23_result, DistUInt{3}(1), x29_result)
     end
     x31_result = x22_result === true ? DistUInt{3}(0) : x22_result === false ? x30_result : ifelse(x22_result, DistUInt{3}(0), x30_result)
    end
    x32_result = x20_finished === true ? x31_result : x20_finished === false ? DistUInt{3}(5) : ifelse(x20_finished, x31_result, DistUInt{3}(5))
    return x32_result
end

function report(k, x, d)
    if x isa AnyBool
        println("alea ", k, " true ", d[true])
        println("alea ", k, " false ", d[false])
    else
        for v in 0:(2^width(x) - 1)
            println("alea ", k, " ", v, " ", d[v])
        end
    end
end

function run_program()
    EV[] = true
    stats = @timed begin
        comps = components(dice_main())
        dists = pr(comps...; evidence = EV[])
        (comps, length(comps) == 1 ? [dists] : dists)
    end
    comps, dists = stats.value
    for k in eachindex(comps)
        report(k, comps[k], dists[k])
    end
    println("alea_seconds ", stats.time)
    println("alea_compile_seconds ", get(stats, :compile_time, NaN))
end

warmup()
task = Task(run_program, 1 << 30)
schedule(task)
wait(task)
end

end

function report(k, x, d)
    if x isa AnyBool
        println("alea ", k, " true ", d[true])
        println("alea ", k, " false ", d[false])
    else
        for v in 0:(2^width(x) - 1)

    end

    EV[] = true
    stats = @timed begin
        comps = components(dice_main())
        dists = pr(comps...; evidence = EV[])
        (comps, length(comps) == 1 ? [dists] : dists)

        report(k, comps[k], dists[k])
    end
    println("alea_seconds ", stats.time)
    println("alea_compile_seconds ", get(stats, :compile_time, NaN))
end

warmup()
task = Task(run_program, 1 << 30)
schedule(task)
wait(task)
end

# rl_hardware_30.dice, translated by tddlog's scripts/dice2alea.py.
module AleaProgram
using Alea
# Julia would spend more time optimizing the long straight-line functions
# below than running them takes: they are interpreted, and Alea's own
# methods compile as usual.
Base.Experimental.@compiler_options compile=min optimize=0 infer=false

const EV = Ref{AnyBool}(true)
observe!(path, c) = (EV[] = EV[] & (!path | c); true)

function shr(x::DistUInt{W}, n::Integer) where W
    k = min(n, W)
    DistUInt{W}(vcat(fill(false, k), x.bits[1:W - k]))
end

components(x::Tuple) = reduce(vcat, map(components, x); init = Any[])
components(x) = Any[x]
width(::DistUInt{W}) where W = W

function warmup()
    a = flip(0.7)
    x = discrete(DistUInt{2}, [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4])
    y = uniform(DistUInt{3}, 1, 6)
    z = ifelse(a, x + DistUInt{2}(1), x - DistUInt{2}(1))
    t = ifelse(flip(0.4), (a, z), (!a, x * x))
    e = prob_equals(z, DistUInt{2}(2)) | (x < z) | xor(a, flip(0.2))
    pr(flip(0.7))
    pr(a, z, y, t...; evidence = e)
    nothing
end

function d_step(x1_path, x2_s)
    x3_t = x2_s[1]
    x4_c = x2_s[2][1]
    x5_running = x2_s[2][2][1]
    x6_finished = x2_s[2][2][2][1]
    x7_r = x2_s[2][2][2][2]
    x8_d = flip(0.0001)
    x9_d = x8_d === true ? DistUInt{2}(0) : x8_d === false ? x4_c : ifelse(x8_d, DistUInt{2}(0), x4_c)
    x10_x = (x5_running & prob_equals(x9_d, DistUInt{2}(0)))
    x11_r2 = x10_x === true ? x3_t : x10_x === false ? x7_r : ifelse(x10_x, x3_t, x7_r)
    x12_u = flip(0.0001)
    x13_u = x12_u === true ? DistUInt{2}(0) : x12_u === false ? x3_t : ifelse(x12_u, DistUInt{2}(0), x3_t)
    x14_g = flip(0.0001)
    x15_g = x14_g === true ? DistUInt{2}(0) : x14_g === false ? x9_d : ifelse(x14_g, DistUInt{2}(0), x9_d)
    x16_f = flip(0.0001)
    x17_f = x16_f === true ? DistUInt{2}(0) : x16_f === false ? x15_g : ifelse(x16_f, DistUInt{2}(0), x15_g)
    x18_step = ((x13_u + x15_g), ((x17_f + DistUInt{2}(1)), ((x5_running & !(x10_x)), ((x6_finished | x10_x), x11_r2))))
    return x18_step
end

function dice_main()
    x19_s = (DistUInt{2}(0), (DistUInt{2}(3), (true, (false, DistUInt{2}(0)))))
    for _ in 1:30
     x19_s = d_step(true, x19_s)
    end
    x20_finished = x19_s[2][2][2][1]
    x21_r = x19_s[2][2][2][2]
    if x20_finished !== false
     x22_result = prob_equals(x21_r, DistUInt{2}(0))
     if x22_result !== true
      x23_result = prob_equals(x21_r, DistUInt{2}(1))
      if x23_result !== true
       x24_result = prob_equals(x21_r, DistUInt{2}(2))
       if x24_result !== true

fun step(s: (int(10), (int(10), (bool, (bool, int(10)))))) {
  let t = fst s in
  let c = fst (snd s) in
  let running = fst (snd (snd s)) in
  let finished = fst (snd (snd (snd s))) in
  let r = snd (snd (snd (snd s))) in
  let d = if flip 0.0001 then int(10, 0) else c in
  let x = running && d == int(10, 0) in
  let r2 = if x then t else r in
  let u = if flip 0.0001 then int(10, 0) else t in
  let g = if flip 0.0001 then int(10, 0) else d in
  let f = if flip 0.0001 then int(10, 0) else g in
  (u + g, (f + int(10, 1), (running && !x, (finished || x, r2))))
}

fun step(s: (int(2), (int(2), (bool, (bool, int(2)))))) {
  let t = fst s in
  let c = fst (snd s) in
  let running = fst (snd (snd s)) in
  let finished = fst (snd (snd (snd s))) in
  let r = snd (snd (snd (snd s))) in
  let d = if flip 0.0001 then int(2, 0) else c in
  let x = running && d == int(2, 0) in
  let r2 = if x then t else r in
  let u = if flip 0.0001 then int(2, 0) else t in
  let g = if flip 0.0001 then int(2, 0) else d in
  let f = if flip 0.0001 then int(2, 0) else g in
  (u + g, (f + int(2, 1), (running && !x, (finished || x, r2))))
}

     x31_result = x22_result === true ? DistUInt{3}(0) : x22_result === false ? x30_result : ifelse(x22_result, DistUInt{3}(0), x30_result)

    x32_result = x20_finished === true ? x31_result : x20_finished === false ? DistUInt{3}(5) : ifelse(x20_finished, x31_result, DistUInt{3}(5))
    return x32_result

function report(k, x, d)
    if x isa AnyBool
        println("alea ", k, " true ", d[true])
        println("alea ", k, " false ", d[false])
    else
        for v in 0:(2^width(x) - 1)
            println("alea ", k, " ", v, " ", d[v])
        end
    end
end

    EV[] = true
    stats = @timed begin
        comps = components(dice_main())
        dists = pr(comps...; evidence = EV[])
        (comps, length(comps) == 1 ? [dists] : dists)
    end
    comps, dists = stats.value
    for k in eachindex(comps)
        report(k, comps[k], dists[k])
    end
    println("alea_seconds ", stats.time)
    println("alea_compile_seconds ", get(stats, :compile_time, NaN))

% loop over a memory of two cells of $2 bits, the total and the counter,
% whose every read first resets the cell to 0 with probability 0.0001
% (z(J, R) before the R-th read of iteration J), running `tri n`: the
% counter starts at $3 (n as `(int n)` holds it in $2 bits), then while
% the counter is not 0, total := total + counter and counter := counter +
% 1, for at most $4 iterations, the fuel; entered with none left, the loop
% ends the run with no result. The cells are bit vectors as Roulette's,
% their set bits atoms: t(J, K) and c(J, K), bit K of the total and the
% counter entering iteration J, on(J) while the loop runs, x(J) when it
% leaves at iteration J. The reads: d (the counter, its test), u (the
% total), g (the counter, its sum), f (the counter, its step). The sums
% ripple their carries up to bit $2 - 1 and drop the last, as bvadd does:
% tx and tc are the total's bit without the carry and the carry into it,
% cc the counter's carry. The queries, consulted from $1 with the totals a
% run can end with (total/1), are res(T) for each of them and res(L), L
% one past the largest, for a run out of fuel (out_of_fuel/1).
% The totals a run of hardware.rkt can end with (the reference's states), the label
% of a run out of fuel, one past the largest, and the queries.
total(0).
total(1).
total(2).
total(3).
out_of_fuel(4).
query(res(0)).
query(res(1)).
query(res(2)).
query(res(3)).
query(res(4)).
width(2).
start(3).
fuel(100).
step(0) :- fuel(F), F > 0.

0.0001::z(J, 4) :- step(J).

number_read(T) :- total(T).
digits(X, 0, X) :- number_read(X).
digits(X, K1, R1) :- digits(X, K, R), R > 1, K1 is K + 1, R1 is R // 2.
one(X, K) :- digits(X, K, R), R mod 2 =:= 1.
c(0, K) :- start(C), one(C, K).
on(0).
d(J, K) :- step(J), c(J, K), \+z(J, 1).
nz(J) :- d(J, _).
x(J) :- step(J), on(J), \+nz(J).
on(J1) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, on(J), nz(J).
u(J, K) :- step(J), t(J, K), \+z(J, 2).
g(J, K) :- d(J, K), \+z(J, 3).
f(J, K) :- g(J, K), \+z(J, 4).
% the total := u + g
tx(J1, K) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, u(J, K), \+g(J, K).
tx(J1, K) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, g(J, K), \+u(J, K).
tc(J1, K1) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, u(J, K), g(J, K), K1 is K + 1, width(W), K1 < W.
tc(J, K1) :- tc(J, K), tx(J, K), K1 is K + 1, width(W), K1 < W.
t(J, K) :- tx(J, K), \+tc(J, K).
t(J, K) :- tc(J, K), \+tx(J, K).
% the counter := f + 1
c(J1, 0) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, \+f(J, 0).
cc(J1, 1) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, f(J, 0), width(W), 1 < W.
cc(J, K1) :- cc(J, K), P is J - 1, f(P, K), K1 is K + 1, width(W), K1 < W.
c(J1, K) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, f(J, K), K > 0, \+cc(J1, K).
c(J, K) :- cc(J, K), P is J - 1, \+f(P, K).

r(K) :- x(J), t(J, K).
mismatch(T) :- total(T), one(T, K), \+r(K).

# rl_hardware_1000.dice, translated by tddlog's scripts/dice2alea.py.
module AleaProgram
using Alea
# Julia would spend more time optimizing the long straight-line functions
# below than running them takes: they are interpreted, and Alea's own
# methods compile as usual.
Base.Experimental.@compiler_options compile=min optimize=0 infer=false

const EV = Ref{AnyBool}(true)
observe!(path, c) = (EV[] = EV[] & (!path | c); true)

function shr(x::DistUInt{W}, n::Integer) where W
    k = min(n, W)
    DistUInt{W}(vcat(fill(false, k), x.bits[1:W - k]))
end

components(x::Tuple) = reduce(vcat, map(components, x); init = Any[])
components(x) = Any[x]
width(::DistUInt{W}) where W = W

function warmup()
    a = flip(0.7)
    x = discrete(DistUInt{2}, [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4])
    y = uniform(DistUInt{3}, 1, 6)
    z = ifelse(a, x + DistUInt{2}(1), x - DistUInt{2}(1))
    t = ifelse(flip(0.4), (a, z), (!a, x * x))
    e = prob_equals(z, DistUInt{2}(2)) | (x < z) | xor(a, flip(0.2))
    pr(flip(0.7))
    pr(a, z, y, t...; evidence = e)
    nothing
end

function d_step(x1_path, x2_s)
    x3_t = x2_s[1]
    x4_c = x2_s[2][1]
    x5_running = x2_s[2][2][1]
    x6_finished = x2_s[2][2][2][1]
    x7_r = x2_s[2][2][2][2]
    x8_d = flip(0.0001)
    x9_d = x8_d === true ? DistUInt{2}(0) : x8_d === false ? x4_c : ifelse(x8_d, DistUInt{2}(0), x4_c)
    x10_x = (x5_running & prob_equals(x9_d, DistUInt{2}(0)))
    x11_r2 = x10_x === true ? x3_t : x10_x === false ? x7_r : ifelse(x10_x, x3_t, x7_r)
    x12_u = flip(0.0001)
    x13_u = x12_u === true ? DistUInt{2}(0) : x12_u === false ? x3_t : ifelse(x12_u, DistUInt{2}(0), x3_t)
    x14_g = flip(0.0001)
    x15_g = x14_g === true ? DistUInt{2}(0) : x14_g === false ? x9_d : ifelse(x14_g, DistUInt{2}(0), x9_d)
    x16_f = flip(0.0001)
    x17_f = x16_f === true ? DistUInt{2}(0) : x16_f === false ? x15_g : ifelse(x16_f, DistUInt{2}(0), x15_g)
    x18_step = ((x13_u + x15_g), ((x17_f + DistUInt{2}(1)), ((x5_running & !(x10_x)), ((x6_finished | x10_x), x11_r2))))
    return x18_step
end

function dice_main()
    x19_s = (DistUInt{2}(0), (DistUInt{2}(3), (true, (false, DistUInt{2}(0)))))
    for _ in 1:1000
     x19_s = d_step(true, x19_s)
    end
    x20_finished = x19_s[2][2][2][1]
    x21_r = x19_s[2][2][2][2]
    if x20_finished !== false
     x22_result = prob_equals(x21_r, DistUInt{2}(0))
     if x22_result !== true
      x23_result = prob_equals(x21_r, DistUInt{2}(1))
      if x23_result !== true
       x24_result = prob_equals(x21_r, DistUInt{2}(2))
       if x24_result !== true
        x25_result = prob_equals(x21_r, DistUInt{2}(3))
        x26_result = x25_result === true ? DistUInt{3}(3) : x25_result === false ? DistUInt{3}(4) : ifelse(x25_result, DistUInt{3}(3), DistUInt{3}(4))
       end
       x27_result = x24_result === true ? DistUInt{3}(2) : x24_result === false ? x26_result : ifelse(x24_result, DistUInt{3}(2), x26_result)
      end
      x28_result = x23_result === true ? DistUInt{3}(1) : x23_result === false ? x27_result : ifelse(x23_result, DistUInt{3}(1), x27_result)
     end
     x29_result = x22_result === true ? DistUInt{3}(0) : x22_result === false ? x28_result : ifelse(x22_result, DistUInt{3}(0), x28_result)
    end
    x30_result = x20_finished === true ? x29_result : x20_finished === false ? DistUInt{3}(4) : ifelse(x20_finished, x29_result, DistUInt{3}(4))
    return x30_result
end

function report(k, x, d)
    if x isa AnyBool
        println("alea ", k, " true ", d[true])
        println("alea ", k, " false ", d[false])
    else
        for v in 0:(2^width(x) - 1)
            println("alea ", k, " ", v, " ", d[v])
        end
    end
end

function run_program()
    EV[] = true
    stats = @timed begin
        comps = components(dice_main())
        dists = pr(comps...; evidence = EV[])
        (comps, length(comps) == 1 ? [dists] : dists)
    end
    comps, dists = stats.value
    for k in eachindex(comps)
        report(k, comps[k], dists[k])
    end
    println("alea_seconds ", stats.time)
    println("alea_compile_seconds ", get(stats, :compile_time, NaN))
end

warmup()
task = Task(run_program, 1 << 30)
schedule(task)
wait(task)
end

    a = flip(0.7)

    x4_c = x2_s[2][1]
    x5_running = x2_s[2][2][1]
    x6_finished = x2_s[2][2][2][1]
    x7_r = x2_s[2][2][2][2]

    x13_u = x12_u === true ? DistUInt{30000}(0) : x12_u === false ? x3_t : ifelse(x12_u, DistUInt{30000}(0), x3_t)
    x14_g = flip(0.0001)

# rl_hardware_bitwidth_300.dice, translated by tddlog's scripts/dice2alea.py.
module AleaProgram
using Alea
# Julia would spend more time optimizing the long straight-line functions
# below than running them takes: they are interpreted, and Alea's own
# methods compile as usual.
Base.Experimental.@compiler_options compile=min optimize=0 infer=false

const EV = Ref{AnyBool}(true)
observe!(path, c) = (EV[] = EV[] & (!path | c); true)

function shr(x::DistUInt{W}, n::Integer) where W
    k = min(n, W)
    DistUInt{W}(vcat(fill(false, k), x.bits[1:W - k]))
end

components(x::Tuple) = reduce(vcat, map(components, x); init = Any[])
components(x) = Any[x]
width(::DistUInt{W}) where W = W

function warmup()
    a = flip(0.7)
    x = discrete(DistUInt{2}, [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4])
    y = uniform(DistUInt{3}, 1, 6)
    z = ifelse(a, x + DistUInt{2}(1), x - DistUInt{2}(1))
    t = ifelse(flip(0.4), (a, z), (!a, x * x))
    e = prob_equals(z, DistUInt{2}(2)) | (x < z) | xor(a, flip(0.2))
    pr(flip(0.7))
    pr(a, z, y, t...; evidence = e)
    nothing
end

function d_step(x1_path, x2_s)
    x3_t = x2_s[1]
    x4_c = x2_s[2][1]
    x5_running = x2_s[2][2][1]
    x6_finished = x2_s[2][2][2][1]
    x7_r = x2_s[2][2][2][2]
    x8_d = flip(0.0001)
    x9_d = x8_d === true ? DistUInt{300}(0) : x8_d === false ? x4_c : ifelse(x8_d, DistUInt{300}(0), x4_c)
    x10_x = (x5_running & prob_equals(x9_d, DistUInt{300}(0)))
    x11_r2 = x10_x === true ? x3_t : x10_x === false ? x7_r : ifelse(x10_x, x3_t, x7_r)
    x12_u = flip(0.0001)
    x13_u = x12_u === true ? DistUInt{300}(0) : x12_u === false ? x3_t : ifelse(x12_u, DistUInt{300}(0), x3_t)
    x14_g = flip(0.0001)
    x15_g = x14_g === true ? DistUInt{300}(0) : x14_g === false ? x9_d : ifelse(x14_g, DistUInt{300}(0), x9_d)
    x16_f = flip(0.0001)
    x17_f = x16_f === true ? DistUInt{300}(0) : x16_f === false ? x15_g : ifelse(x16_f, DistUInt{300}(0), x15_g)
    x18_step = ((x13_u + x15_g), ((x17_f + DistUInt{300}(1)), ((x5_running & !(x10_x)), ((x6_finished | x10_x), x11_r2))))
    return x18_step
end

function dice_main()
    x19_s = (DistUInt{300}(0), (DistUInt{300}(2), (true, (false, DistUInt{300}(0)))))
    for _ in 1:3
     x19_s = d_step(true, x19_s)
    end
    x20_finished = x19_s[2][2][2][1]
    x21_r = x19_s[2][2][2][2]
    if x20_finished !== false
     x22_result = prob_equals(x21_r, DistUInt{300}(0))
     if x22_result !== true
      x23_result = prob_equals(x21_r, DistUInt{300}(1))
      if x23_result !== true
       x24_result = prob_equals(x21_r, DistUInt{300}(2))
       if x24_result !== true
        x25_result = prob_equals(x21_r, DistUInt{300}(3))
        if x25_result !== true
         x26_result = prob_equals(x21_r, DistUInt{300}(5))
         x27_result = x26_result === true ? DistUInt{3}(4) : x26_result === false ? DistUInt{3}(5) : ifelse(x26_result, DistUInt{3}(4), DistUInt{3}(5))
        end
        x28_result = x25_result === true ? DistUInt{3}(3) : x25_result === false ? x27_result : ifelse(x25_result, DistUInt{3}(3), x27_result)
       end
       x29_result = x24_result === true ? DistUInt{3}(2) : x24_result === false ? x28_result : ifelse(x24_result, DistUInt{3}(2), x28_result)
      end
      x30_result = x23_result === true ? DistUInt{3}(1) : x23_result === false ? x29_result : ifelse(x23_result, DistUInt{3}(1), x29_result)
     end
     x31_result = x22_result === true ? DistUInt{3}(0) : x22_result === false ? x30_result : ifelse(x22_result, DistUInt{3}(0), x30_result)
    end
    x32_result = x20_finished === true ? x31_result : x20_finished === false ? DistUInt{3}(5) : ifelse(x20_finished, x31_result, DistUInt{3}(5))
    return x32_result
end

function report(k, x, d)
    if x isa AnyBool
        println("alea ", k, " true ", d[true])
        println("alea ", k, " false ", d[false])
    else
        for v in 0:(2^width(x) - 1)
            println("alea ", k, " ", v, " ", d[v])
        end
    end
end

function run_program()
    EV[] = true
    stats = @timed begin
        comps = components(dice_main())
        dists = pr(comps...; evidence = EV[])
        (comps, length(comps) == 1 ? [dists] : dists)
    end
    comps, dists = stats.value
    for k in eachindex(comps)
        report(k, comps[k], dists[k])
    end
    println("alea_seconds ", stats.time)
    println("alea_compile_seconds ", get(stats, :compile_time, NaN))
end

warmup()
task = Task(run_program, 1 << 30)
schedule(task)
wait(task)
end

% The interpreter of Roulette's scaling/hardware.rkt, ported to ProbLog: a
% loop over a memory of two cells of $2 bits, the total and the counter,
% whose every read first resets the cell to 0 with probability 0.0001
% (z(J, R) before the R-th read of iteration J), running `tri n`: the
% counter starts at $3 (n as `(int n)` holds it in $2 bits), then while
% the counter is not 0, total := total + counter and counter := counter +
% 1, for at most $4 iterations, the fuel; entered with none left, the loop
% ends the run with no result. The cells are bit vectors as Roulette's,
% their set bits atoms: t(J, K) and c(J, K), bit K of the total and the
% counter entering iteration J, on(J) while the loop runs, x(J) when it
% leaves at iteration J. The reads: d (the counter, its test), u (the
% total), g (the counter, its sum), f (the counter, its step). The sums
% ripple their carries up to bit $2 - 1 and drop the last, as bvadd does:
% tx and tc are the total's bit without the carry and the carry into it,
% cc the counter's carry. The queries, consulted from $1 with the totals a
% run can end with (total/1), are res(T) for each of them and res(L), L
% one past the largest, for a run out of fuel (out_of_fuel/1).
:- consult($1).
width($2).
start($3).
fuel($4).
step(0) :- fuel(F), F > 0.
step(J1) :- step(J), fuel(F), J1 is J + 1, J1 < F.
0.0001::z(J, 1) :- step(J).
0.0001::z(J, 2) :- step(J).
0.0001::z(J, 3) :- step(J).
0.0001::z(J, 4) :- step(J).
% one(X, K): bit K of the number X is set, for the numbers the program reads
number_read(C) :- start(C).
number_read(T) :- total(T).
digits(X, 0, X) :- number_read(X).
digits(X, K1, R1) :- digits(X, K, R), R > 1, K1 is K + 1, R1 is R // 2.
one(X, K) :- digits(X, K, R), R mod 2 =:= 1.
c(0, K) :- start(C), one(C, K).
on(0).
d(J, K) :- step(J), c(J, K), \+z(J, 1).
nz(J) :- d(J, _).
x(J) :- step(J), on(J), \+nz(J).
on(J1) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, on(J), nz(J).
u(J, K) :- step(J), t(J, K), \+z(J, 2).
g(J, K) :- d(J, K), \+z(J, 3).
f(J, K) :- g(J, K), \+z(J, 4).
% the total := u + g
tx(J1, K) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, u(J, K), \+g(J, K).
tx(J1, K) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, g(J, K), \+u(J, K).
tc(J1, K1) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, u(J, K), g(J, K), K1 is K + 1, width(W), K1 < W.
tc(J, K1) :- tc(J, K), tx(J, K), K1 is K + 1, width(W), K1 < W.
t(J, K) :- tx(J, K), \+tc(J, K).
t(J, K) :- tc(J, K), \+tx(J, K).
% the counter := f + 1
c(J1, 0) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, \+f(J, 0).
cc(J1, 1) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, f(J, 0), width(W), 1 < W.
cc(J, K1) :- cc(J, K), P is J - 1, f(P, K), K1 is K + 1, width(W), K1 < W.
c(J1, K) :- step(J), J1 is J + 1, f(J, K), K > 0, \+cc(J1, K).
c(J, K) :- cc(J, K), P is J - 1, \+f(P, K).
% the total the loop left with, and whether it is T
done :- x(_).
r(K) :- x(J), t(J, K).
mismatch(T) :- total(T), one(T, K), \+r(K).
mismatch(T) :- total(T), r(K), \+one(T, K).
res(T) :- total(T), done, \+mismatch(T).
res(L) :- out_of_fuel(L), fuel(F), on(F).
